nonblocking_findings: Printed p.262 (image 264) and p.263 (image 265): each page has two short horizontal rules stacked with nothing between them. It looks like an empty divider or an empty block is being drawn. This is cosmetic only: nothing is clipped or overlapping.

Printed p.263 (image 265): the English heading 'The cantor repeats according to the community's custom; on weekdays some do not re-peat.' is hyphenated so that 'peat.' sits alone on its own right-aligned line. It's readable but awkward. Turning off hyphenation in rubric headings would fix it.

Printed p.261 (image 263): footnote 137 ('נוסח אחר') prints at the bottom right of the page, but its separator rule is under the Hebrew column on the left. The superscript marker on 'כמצוה' is readable and the note is on the same page as its marker. This is a small placement difference, not a defect.
verdict: I read all six assigned page images (printed pp.261–266) and the manifest. Nothing is clipped, and no text or columns overlap. The Hebrew, with its vowel points, and the English are both clean and readable. The paired Hebrew/English stanza rows line up across pp.261–265. That includes the Shofaroth verse rows, Hayom Harat Olam (once for the congregation, once for the cantor), Areshet Sefatenu (also both), Retzei, Vete'erav, the 'when there is no priestly blessing' variant, Modim and Modim deRabbanan, Ukhtov, Vekhol Hahayyim, and the Elohenu ve-Elohei Avotenu introduction to the priestly blessing. Footnote 137 is on the same page as its marker and is labelled. Hebrew and English rubrics, and the קהל/חזן speaker labels, appear wherever expected. On p.265 the batch ends at the priestly-blessing introduction, before the verses. The missing-source label there is clear in both languages and names scan311 as where encoding stops and scan312 as where the unencoded part begins. The metadata on p.266 is intact: the CC BY-SA 4.0 and CC0 licenses with their URLs, contributor credits (Codex; Efraim Feinstein), and a complete Sources entry [1] for Birnbaum 1949 with archive.org links. The only findings are the three small cosmetic ones listed. Approved.
